# hax-lab

> HAX Lab: learn web development by shipping real HAX work, from onboarding to your first contribution

HAXcms is a file-based CMS: authored pages and metadata are stored as portable files, not locked into a database-only workflow.
The canonical site structure is `site.json`, represented in JSON Outline Schema (`id`, `parent`, `order`, `slug`, `location`, and `metadata`).
Use HAX CLI and ecosystem tooling to maintain human-authored content while keeping machine-readable outputs synchronized.
Managed files (feeds, search indexes, manifests, and this `llms.txt`) are generated artifacts and should be rebuilt by tooling.

## Core resources
- [site.json](https://lab.hax.cloud/site.json): Canonical site manifest and navigation tree in JSON Outline Schema format.
- [llms.txt](https://lab.hax.cloud/llms.txt): LLM-oriented guide to this site and its machine-readable resources.
- [llms-full.txt](https://lab.hax.cloud/llms-full.txt): The whole site as one markdown document, in outline order.
- [Whole site as HTML](https://lab.hax.cloud/x/api/v1/site/export/html): Every page in one HTML document.
- [AGENTS.md](https://lab.hax.cloud/AGENTS.md): Instructions for AI agents working on this site's files.

## Pages
- [HAX Lab](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-home/index.md): HAX Lab is where students and junior developers learn web development by shipping real work in HAX, the open source web publishing platform built at Penn State.
- [How this course works](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-how-this-course-works/index.md): Every topic is one page. Each page takes about 10 to 20 minutes of reading or watching, then about an hour of doing.
- [How HAX Lab works](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-how-hax-lab-works/index.md): HAX Lab is one part of a loop.
- [1. How the web works](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-how-the-web-works/index.md): Before you write any code, you'll see what the web is doing when you click a link, and set up the accounts and tools every other page assumes.
- [What happens when you load a page](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-what-happens-when-you-load-a-page/index.md): A website is a conversation. Your browser asks for something, a server somewhere answers with text, and the browser turns that text into what you see.
- [Accounts you'll need](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-accounts/index.md): Professional web developers live in a handful of free services.
- [Install your tools](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-install-your-tools/index.md): This is the page where most people get stuck, so go slowly. You'll install the same tools working developers use: a runtime for JavaScript, version control, an editor, and the HAX command line.
- [Onboarding](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-onboarding/index.md): HAX Lab onboarding is for students and junior developers. It takes you from knowing nothing about how websites are built to opening your first contribution to HAX, an open source web publishing project used across Penn State and beyond.
- [2. Web components](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-web-components/index.md): Web components let you invent your own HTML tags. They're built into every modern browser, so code you write today keeps working long after the framework of the year is gone.
- [What are web components](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-what-are-web-components/index.md): For years every web framework invented its own idea of a "component", and every one of them only worked inside that framework.
- [Project 1: a card in CodePen](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-codepen-card/index.md): Your first project is small on purpose: rebuild one video card from YouTube in plain HTML and CSS.
- [Project 1b: a second card](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-second-card/index.md): Now make a different card that shares the first one's DNA. Maybe it's the channel card that sits next to videos, or a playlist card.
- [3. Design systems](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-design-systems/index.md): A design system is a set of decisions made once, so nobody has to make them again: colors, spacing, type, corner radius, how a button looks when you hover it.
- [Design systems and DDD](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-design-systems-and-ddd/index.md): Every color, gap and font size in HAX comes from a token: a named CSS variable like --ddd-spacing-4.
- [4. Real development](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-real-development/index.md): CodePen was training wheels. Now your card becomes a real web component in a real project folder on your computer, styled with DDD, checked with audit tools, saved in GitHub and published by Vercel every time you push.
- [npm and hax webcomponent](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-npm-and-hax-webcomponent/index.md): Nobody writes everything from scratch.
- [Port your card](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-port-your-card/index.md): Move your CodePen card into my-card.js. The parts that changed from card to card become properties.
- [GitHub and Vercel](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-github-and-vercel/index.md): Your card only exists on your computer. In this step it goes to GitHub, where your history and your portfolio live, and Vercel watches that repository and publishes a fresh build every time you push.
- [5. Data-driven cards](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-data-driven-cards/index.md): Real cards don't have their content typed into HTML. YouTube's cards come from data.
- [Content modeling and JSON](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-content-modeling-json/index.md): Content modeling means deciding what your data looks like before you write any of it: which fields a card has, what type each one is, and which are required.
- [Fetch and render, with AI](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-fetch-and-render/index.md): Your element will now load cards.json itself and draw a card for every item.
- [Card controls, without AI](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-card-controls/index.md): Close the AI tab. This page is yours alone, because this is the skill everything else depends on: find an element, listen for a user, check a rule, change the page.
- [6. Into HAX](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-into-hax/index.md): You can now do what new HAX contributors do in their first weeks: read code, build an element, ship it, and change data with confidence.
- [What HAX is and how it works](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-what-is-hax/index.md): HAX is a way to make websites without thinking about it, in a format that keeps working.
- [Hack this course](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-hack-this-course/index.md): The site you're reading is a folder of files in a public GitHub repository.
- [Find your first issue](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-first-issue/index.md): Every bug, idea and task for every HAX repository lives in one place: the unified issue queue.
- [Capstone: your own HAX site](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-capstone/index.md): No steps this time, just the goal and the checkpoints. Make a HAX site in your browser, bind it to a folder on your computer, change it with the hax command line, put it in GitHub and publish it.
- [Next: join HAX Lab](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-next-steps/index.md): You're onboarded. You know how a request works, how to build and ship a web component, how to drive it with data, and how a HAX site goes from your keyboard to the world.
- [SIIP: how a course becomes a pipeline](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-siip/index.md): SIIP, the Sustainable Impact and Innovation Pipeline, turns a course into a contributor pipeline for an open source project without turning the course into "the project class".
- [Graduates](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-graduates/index.md): Everyone the HAX Lab roster credits, newest first, each drawn as the character HAX would give them.
- [Faculty and funding](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-faculty-and-funding/index.md): Faculty fund student work that solves their own problems, and HAX gains the capability for everyone.
- [Outcomes](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-outcomes/index.md): Lab work counts twice: once in what HAX can do for everyone, and again in what the students can do next.
- [About](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-962104ee-d156-4595-8a92-ae14d56a198f/index.md): What this site is and who makes it.
- [Contact](https://lab.hax.cloud/pages/item-0480f9b7-9ee4-4919-b30e-7df5b6461ff0/index.md): How to reach the people who make HAX.

- [HAX skill catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/haxtheweb/praw/stable/skills/index.json): Every HAX agent skill, maintained in PRAW; fetch skills this site does not ship from here.
